## 3400 N Central Park Ave — Zoning & Development Assessment
**PIN:** 13233160400000 | **Parcel Resolution:** Authoritative

---

### 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **RS-3 (Residential Single-Unit)** per the City's official GIS system. RS-3 is the most common single-family district, primarily accommodating detached houses on individual lots, though two-flats and limited multi-unit buildings are also permitted at appropriate densities [3].

**Verify:** [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning)

---

### 2. Could You Build a Two-Flat?

**Probably yes, but it depends on block context.** The lot is 3,616 sq ft. The base RS-3 minimum lot area per unit is 2,500 sq ft [1], which by lot area alone yields only 1 unit (3,616 ÷ 2,500 = 1.4 → 1 unit). A two-flat would require 5,000 sq ft at base standards.

However, [1] provides a key exemption: in RS-3, the minimum lot area per unit **may be reduced to 1,500 sq ft** (allowing a two-unit building only) when either:
- 60% or more of the lots fronting the same block face are already improved with buildings containing more than one unit, **or**
- The property falls within the "Predominance of the Block" boundaries under §17-7-0591.

At 1,500 sq ft/unit, a two-flat would require only 3,000 sq ft — well within this lot's 3,616 sq ft. So **if the block-face condition is met, a two-flat is permitted by right** under [1]. You would need to verify the block-face composition.

Additionally, ground-floor Type A accessible units are exempt from the lot-area-per-unit count in RS-3 [1].

**Note:** Lot area is only one constraint. FAR (0.9), height (30 ft), parking, and lot configuration can further limit what's buildable [1].

**Verify:** Survey the block face for multi-unit buildings, or consult the Department of Zoning & Land Use Planning.

---

### 3. Key Bulk & Density Standards

All figures from the RS-3 zoning table [3] / [1]:

| Standard | RS-3 Requirement |
|---|---|
| **FAR** | 0.9 |
| **Max Height** | 30 ft |
| **Min Lot Area** | 2,500 sq ft |
| **Min Lot Area/Unit** | 2,500 sq ft (reducible to 1,500 for 2-unit; see §2 above) |
| **Min Lot Width** | Not confirmed in retrieved data |
| **Setbacks** | Not confirmed in retrieved data |

Setback and lot-width figures were not in the retrieved code text — confirm at [§17-2-0400](https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/dcd/provdrs/zoning.html) or via the Zoning Map.

---

### 4. Overlays & Special Designations

- **Transit-Oriented Development (CTA):** This parcel is in a CTA TOD area — the Addison Blue Line station is approximately 0.25 miles away [overlay data]. This has parking implications (see §5).
- **ADU Eligible Area:** This parcel falls within a designated Additional Dwelling Unit-Allowed RS Area [2], meaning coach houses and conversion units may be permissible (see §6).
- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone:** Any qualifying development may trigger ARO obligations. The Avondale community area has 6 ARO-related affordable housing projects totaling 76 units, including Milwaukee Ave. Apts. (32 units) and Hairpin Lofts (25 units).
- **Special District:** The parcel is within a Special District designation; the specific restrictions were not detailed in the retrieved documents — verify with the Department of Zoning.
- **No Planned Development**, no landmark or historic district designation, no lakefront protection, no Special Service Area, and no PMD apply [regulatory data].
- **Flood Zone X:** FEMA designates this parcel as an Area of Minimal Flood Hazard — not a Special Flood Hazard Area; flood insurance is not required [regulatory data].
- **Brownfields nearby:** Two BNSF Little Village Paseo sites (EPA IDs 110071982538 and 110071982539) are in the general area. Environmental due diligence may be advisable for any ground-disturbing work.

---

### 5. Parking Requirement & Transit Reduction

Off-street parking in RS districts must be located on the same lot as the units served [5], and is prohibited in side setbacks or within 20 feet of the front property line [5].

Because this parcel is in a **CTA TOD area**, the minimum parking requirement **may be reduced by up to 100%** under §17-10-0102-B — meaning parking could potentially be waived entirely for residential uses. This is parking relief only; **no FAR, height, or density bonus applies** in RS-3 (those apply only in "dash-3" B, C, or D districts) [tod_benefits data / §17-10-0102-B].

---

### 6. Coach House / ADU

**Yes — this parcel is in an ADU-eligible area**, and coach houses in RS districts are specifically governed by [2] and [4]:

Key conditions under [4]:
- A **building permit for a new coach house in an RS district** may only be issued if the lot complies with [2] (the ADU Eligible Areas ordinance).
- The coach house may **not exceed 22 feet in building height** [4].
- Rooftop features may not exceed 22 feet above grade [4].
- At least **3 feet of unobstructed open space** must be maintained between the coach house and at least one side property line for the full length of the building wall (except where the side lot line abuts an alley or street) [4].
- **Accessory parking for the principal building may be reduced or waived** via administrative adjustment [4]; the coach house itself requires no accessory parking [4].
- In B or C districts a coach house must be in the rear 30 feet — but this parcel is RS-3, so that restriction doesn't apply [4].

Under [2], each ADU-Allowed RS Area may impose additional limitations on conversion units and coach houses. You would need to verify the specific limitations applicable to Avondale's ADU area designation.

**Enforcement** of ADU eligibility is handled by the Department of Housing at the time of ADU pre-certification [2].

**Verify:** Contact the Department of Housing (ADU program) and review §17-7-0574 for area-specific limits.

---

### Confidence & Limitations

**High confidence:** Zoning classification, FAR, max height, lot area per unit, overlay designations, TOD parking relief, coach house height/setback limits — all drawn from authoritative GIS and code data.

**Moderate confidence:** Two-flat feasibility — depends on block-face composition that cannot be verified remotely; the lot-area math is clear but the triggering condition requires a field survey or city confirmation.

**Could not determine:** Specific side/rear/front setback dimensions (not in retrieved code text), specific ADU area limitations for Avondale under §17-7-0574, and the precise nature of the "Special District" designation.
